title: Gambhir's Coaching Record Under Fire as India's WTC Hopes Fade
excerpt: With 10 defeats in 19 Tests and a win percentage of 36.84%, Gautam Gambhir's tenure as India's head coach faces mounting scrutiny — though the BCCI has signaled it will stick with him through the 2027 World Cup.
body:
• India have won just 7 of 19 Tests under Gambhir, losing 10 with 2 draws — a 36.84% win rate that marks one of India's worst coaching stretches in modern Test cricket
  • Series defeats to New Zealand (3-0), Australia (3-1), and South Africa (2-0) have left India's WTC final hopes in serious jeopardy
  • Former cricketer Amit Mishra has urged patience, saying India should give Gambhir more time to rebuild
  • BCCI has confirmed Gambhir will continue as head coach, with his contract running until the 2027 World Cup

Gautam Gambhir's tenure as India's head coach is under the most intense scrutiny it has faced since he took charge in July 2024. With 10 defeats in 19 Tests, a win percentage of just 36.84%, and India's World Test Championship hopes fading rapidly, calls for a coaching change have grown louder — even as the BCCI maintains its support.

A Record That Tells Its Own Story

The numbers are stark. Under Gambhir, India have been swept 3-0 at home by New Zealand — a result that shook Indian cricket to its core. That was followed by a 3-1 defeat in Australia during the Border-Gavaskar Trophy, ending India's decade-long dominance in that series. Most recently, South Africa inflicted a 2-0 whitewash in India, including a historic 408-run defeat in Guwahati, India's largest loss by runs in Test history.

The cumulative toll: seven wins, 10 losses, and two draws across 19 Tests. For a team that had been the dominant force in Test cricket at home for the better part of two decades, the collapse has been dramatic.

WTC Final Slipping Away

India's position in the WTC 2025-27 cycle has deteriorated with each series loss. Australia lead the standings with an 87.5% points percentage, while India's repeated bilateral defeats have pushed them further from the final. With remaining fixtures offering limited opportunities to recover, India's margin for error has all but disappeared.

The ongoing Australia-Bangladesh series in Darwin further complicates matters. An Australian sweep would consolidate their grip on the top spot, making India's task even more difficult.

"Indian cricket is important, I am not. Only the BCCI will decide whether I should continue."

— Gautam Gambhir, after India's series loss to South Africa

Voices of Support and Criticism

Former India leg-spinner Amit Mishra has urged the cricketing public and the board to give Gambhir more time, arguing that the rebuilding process requires patience. Mishra's position reflects a segment of the cricket establishment that views the current phase as a difficult but necessary transition, with several senior players retiring and a new generation still finding its feet.

Others have been less forgiving. Strategic decisions — including batting order choices, the handling of the bowling rotation, and the team's inability to adapt to conditions abroad — have drawn pointed criticism from former players and analysts. The recent T20I series losses to Ireland and England, resulting in India's first consecutive bilateral T20I series defeats since 2018-19, have added to the pressure, though Gambhir guided India to the 2026 T20 World Cup, Champions Trophy, and Asia Cup titles.

BCCI Backs Gambhir — For Now

Despite the mounting criticism, the BCCI has made clear it is not rushing to a decision. A senior board official told media that there is "no appetite for immediate upheaval," citing Gambhir's contract that runs until the 2027 World Cup. A performance review involving the coaching staff, selectors, and team management is underway, but no change is considered imminent.

Reports have surfaced of VVS Laxman potentially taking on a larger red-ball coaching role, and at least one member of Gambhir's support staff is reportedly in discussions with an IPL franchise. But for now, the BCCI's official position remains one of patience over panic.

What's Next

Gambhir's next major test will come in India's upcoming home assignments, where the team has traditionally been near-invincible. A continued slide at home would make the BCCI's stance increasingly untenable, regardless of white-ball tournament success. For Indian cricket fans, the question is no longer whether Gambhir can turn things around — it's how much longer the board will wait to find out.
